themes.name: Decision load
themes.claim_sentence: As agents take over the work, the decisions left to people become the scarce, tiring part, so teams record them, queue them for a person, and keep them few enough to make well.
themes.definition: Across the talks, agents do more of the doing and people are left with the deciding. Ankit Jain finds that human review comments were mostly about decisions and has agents argue so the decisions surface and get written down. Karan Vaidya's security agents queue uncertain findings for a person to judge in the morning. Scott Tolinski's survey shows the cost: running many agents multiplies the decisions and wears people out, and fewer agents in parallel helps.
themes.why_uncontested: No talk argues decisions can be handed to agents outright; even Karan Vaidya's always-on agents route uncertain cases to a person.

themes.name: Context for AI
themes.claim_sentence: AI does its best work on context people have already curated (the intent captured in a session, modeled data, a map of the database), not on raw systems.
themes.definition: George Fraser's companies connect their agents to the same modeled data stack that serves BI, simplify messy data for them, and give them an agent schema as a map. Ankit Jain captures a change's intent and acceptance criteria from the agent session rather than writing specs. Utkarsh Shrivastava calls the AI tool the tip of the iceberg and puts Netflix's lasting investment in the company context beneath it: enterprise skills and MCP servers. In each, the useful input is something a person already shaped.
themes.why_uncontested: No talk argues agents do better on raw systems than on curated context; whether to reach company data through each app is recorded separately as contested.

themes.name: Guardrails people own
themes.claim_sentence: Agents are trusted through guardrails that people own (rules that check their output, scoped access, and a firewall on what goes in and what they do) rather than by people reading what they produce.
themes.definition: Ankit Jain mines years of review comments into rules with owners and turns some into deterministic checks, so people own the rules instead of the code. Karan Vaidya gives agents broad but granular access to each app and puts a firewall on both their inputs and their actions. Utkarsh Shrivastava has Netflix's domain teams run a regression eval suite in CI before any new connector or model change, and scales the gate with the stakes, from reads to irreversible writes. All three replace line-by-line supervision with controls a named person or team maintains.
themes.why_uncontested: No talk argues for trusting agent output unchecked or for returning to line-by-line review.

themes.name: Connecting is not answering
themes.claim_sentence: Connecting an AI to every source is now cheap, but it does not settle which source answers, so a connection per source produces wrong or conflicting answers unless something decides between them.
themes.definition: George Fraser argues that wiring an assistant to each system of record through MCP fails for data questions because it cannot join across sources. Utkarsh Shrivastava reaches the same problem from inside Netflix: every connector is another way for the agent to choose wrong, two correct connectors gave different viewer counts for one event, and MCP made access cheap without settling who owns the answer. Fraser's fix is one modeled store; Shrivastava's is a platform that gates and arbitrates across domain-owned connectors.

contested.question: Do the skills people built before AI carry over?

sides.stance: Coding skills fade with AI use, and much of what is lost no longer matters
The analytics skills data teams built are exactly what AI context needs

contested.question: Should agents reach company data through each app or through one modeled store?

sides.stance: Through the modeled warehouse; a connection per source cannot join across sources
Through scoped access to each of the company's apps
Through MCP servers each domain owns, behind a shared platform that gates access and decides which source answers
